newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 5.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
CONGRESS DECIDES AGAINST WITHDRAWING SUPPORT TO UF

Congress Working Committee (CWC) flayed the United Front (UF) government for its performance on various fronts including its attitude to the Congress, but decided to continue with its support to the government. On Uttar Pradesh, the CWC decided to persist with its plans to install Bahujan Samaj Party leader Mayawati as the UP chief minister. The party criticised the UF's unwillingness to back Mayawati and asked the 13 party coalition to support the Congress move in UP to keep the Bharatiya Janata Party out.
NEW EXIM POLICY SEES SCOPE FOR FERTILISER PROJECT

The government has enlarged the scope of the deemed export scheme under the current export-import (1992-97) policy. This will be applicable to the fertiliser projects set up in the country. The benefits include refund of terminal excise duty and the special import licence. The scheme will also apply to capital goods supplies to intermediate products like ammonia, phosphoric acid, sulphuric acid and others.
APEX BANK TO ACT AS FACILITATOR FOR EXPORTERS

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) deputy governor R.V. Gupta has called upon the banks to conduct monthly meetings with exporters to promptly redress their grievances. The RBI would henceforth act as a facilitator and not as a policy maker, Gupta said. The RBI deputy governor said the meetings would help to evaluate the efficacy of the monetary policy and initiate corrective steps for a better competitive ability to Indian exports.
FOREIGN BROKERAGES HUNT DOMESTIC FINANCE FIRMS

Foreign stockbroking firms are set to enter the Indian markets in a big way with at least 10 new outfits working out plans for setting up independent brokerages. The names include NatWest Markets, Union Bank of Switzerland, Klienwort Benson, Barclays de Zoete Wedd and CS First Boston. The new entrants are looking for domestic partners since established Indian brokerages are not willing to let them have majority stakes. The foreign players are seeking domestic partners among finance companies or non-resident Indians (NRI) to sell a minority stake in their brokerages. Foreign companies are not allowed to set up l00 percent Indian subsidiaries for stockbroking activities. They must have at least 25 percent Indian or NRI shareholding.
SAMSUNG TO PUMP $1 BLN INTO INDIA

South Korean giant Samsung plans to invest over $1 billion in India to take up its total investment in the country to $2 billion by 2000 AD. The group has identified petrochemicals and automobiles as the new thrust areas for investments in future. The company had received the government's approval to set up a 100 percent-owned holding company and to invest up to $630 million in the consumer electronics and telecommunication sectors. Details as to the exact quantum of investment to be made in each sector is not known as yet.

The government has received yet another indicator of the declining industrial production. Industrial Entrepreneurs' Memoranda (IEM) received during April-September this year projects investments worth 612.83 billion rupees - a sharp fall of 38.55 percent compared to the corresponding period last year. In 1995, India received 997.33 billion rupees worth of IEMs during the same period. As a result employment generation projections in IEMs this year crashed by 35 percent. Although IEMs are not an actual indicator of investment flowing into the country, the fall in IEMs is a sign of declining investor interest in the country.
